messages:
nina: noticed a billing discrepancy report: a handful of customers see higher token usage in the console than what their SDK logs show for the same request set. digging in.
ash: rough numbers?
mike: seeing ~8-12% delta on batched streaming workloads for orgs sending many short prompts in a single request. single-request traffic looks fine.
tara: could be batching normalization. our Go SDK trims trailing newlines before tokenizing but the backend currently normalizes whitespace differently for batched inputs.
ben: TS SDK behavior: we do minimal normalization (single whitespace collapse) but we also merge messages when streaming. that could change token boundaries.
ina: hypothesis: tokenization divergence between client-side estimators (used in cost previews and client logs) and server-side canonical tokenization used for billing. For batched streaming we apply a sentinel joiner that client libs don't simulate.
ash: we need two things: immediate customer-facing mitigations (quick reconciliation API or billing credit if obvious) and a longer-term fix to keep SDKs and server in sync.
mike: agree. ops can issue manual credits where delta >10% and clear reproducible. want a short rollback plan too.
tara: long-term fix options: 1) enforce server-side pre-tokenization policy and expose a client helper `canonicalize_for_token_count(text)` in all SDKs; 2) move token counting to a server-returned header so SDKs always read canonical counts; 3) change batching API to send an array of pre-tokenized segments.
ben: option 2 seems least breaking: server returns X-RW-TOKEN-COUNT per response and SDKs surface that. But logs already show client-estimated counts; customers will still see discrepancy historically until they migrate.
ina: option 1 is more proactive: shipping a canonicalizer in SDKs ensures client logs match server counts. but that's a behavioral change that could affect a ton of existing analytics code if clients rely on old heuristics. needs a deprecation path.
ash: can we do both? server starts returning the canonical counts header now (opt-in flag for canary orgs). SDKs ship a helper and an opt-in flag `use_canonical_tokenizer=true` which toggles canonicalization before estimating locally. default off for existing installs, on for new installs.
tara: we can add a minor-breaking change for the helper signature (since we previously used `estimate_tokens(text)` returning int; new helper returns `{count, normalized_text}` to help audits). that'll be a semver minor bump with clear changelog.
ben: TS/Go parity ok. we'll add a compatibility shim that preserves old function but logs DeprecationWarning. good to limit churn.
ina: console work: add a reconciliation view showing server token-count vs client-estimate per request batch (CSV export) and a flag to show only requests where delta > 5%.
mike: billing: will need a script to backfill credits for last 30 days where server_count > client_estimate by >10% for eligible orgs. ops, can you prepare?
ash: infra note: streaming path currently uses a compact merge protocol where we append `
--batch--
` between prompts. server tokenization treats that separator as 3 tokens; some SDKs strip it when estimating. Fix: server will treat an explicit header `X-RW-BATCH-SEPARATOR` if present and accept client-sent separator string so tokenization matches.
tara: we'll add SDK option `batchSeparator` defaulting to `
--batch--
` and include it in client estimates. that avoids changing existing app text.
ben: add a lint rule to flag apps that manually concatenate prompts without using SDK batch APIs; manual concatenation is risky.
ina: rollout plan: 1) immediate: server will begin emitting X-RW-TOKEN-COUNT in responses for canary orgs (today). 2) SDKs: publish helper and opt-in `use_canonical_tokenizer` in next minor release; keep compat shim for 2 releases. 3) console: reconciliation tile + export in 2 weeks. 4) billing backfill script to run after 2-week monitoring window.
ci-bot: go-sdk 1.9.3-alpha and ts-sdk 3.4.0-beta with `use_canonical_tokenizer` and `batchSeparator` options published to canaries at 2026-04-14T11:45:00Z
mike: support/template: we should prepare customer-facing notes explaining why estimates differ and that canonical counts are authoritative for billing.
tara: tests: unit for canonicalizer, cross-SDK golden fixtures (same inputs should produce identical counts), e2e for streaming batch path. also run a parity test harness against server token counts.
ben: will add a `token-count-golden.jsonl` fixture set to the SDK test suites.
ina: approvals?
mike: ack from billing.
nina: approved, proceeding. I'll create the tracking epic and link PRs.
